Text:
🎃 The missing CSP: anything can crawl in.

Without a Content-Security-Policy header, the browser runs any script that ends up in your page, including one an attacker injected.

Exorcise it: Check your response headers for Content-Security-Policy. Start in report-only mode, read the reports, then enforce it.

🎃 The zombie redirect chain: it keeps coming back.

An old link hops from http to https, then to www, then to a trailing slash. Every hop costs a round trip, and crawlers can stop following a long chain before they reach the page.

Exorcise it: Follow your old links to their final address. Send each one there in a single redirect, and update the links you control.

🎃 The haunted 404: the page is gone, the server says 200.

A missing page that answers 200 OK is a soft 404. Search engines can index the error page, and monitors that only read status codes never see the broken link.

Exorcise it: Open a made-up address on your site. It should answer 404 and offer a way back: a link home and a search box.

🎃 The cursed alt text: IMG_2041.jpg says nothing.

Screen readers read alt text aloud. A file name or the word image leaves the picture a mystery, and a long description on a decorative image wastes the listener's time.

Exorcise it: Go through the images on your top page. Describe the ones that inform, and give decorative ones an empty alt.

🎃 The poltergeist layout shift: the button moved by itself.

Images without dimensions, late ads and swapped fonts push content down while people read and tap. Cumulative Layout Shift measures it, and 0.1 or less counts as good.

Exorcise it: Load your page on a slow connection and watch it settle. Give images a width and height, and reserve space for ads and embeds.
